data.name: FaqTitle
data.value: What people ask before they start

data.name: Faq1A
data.value: No. A chair and a wall are enough for every session. If you have a resistance band, a few sessions use it, and each one says so before you start.

data.name: Faq2Q
data.value: What happens to my streak if I miss a day?

data.name: Faq2A
data.value: Nothing, the first two times in a week. You get two rest days a week: plan them, or Pulsepath uses one when you miss a day. The streak only starts over after a third missed day in the same week.

data.name: Faq3Q
data.value: When is the Android app coming?

data.name: Faq3A
data.value: We plan to release it in January 2027. It's in closed testing with 400 people now. Join the Android waitlist and we'll send one email on release day. Until then, the web app works in Chrome on Android, and you can install it on your home screen.

data.name: Faq4A
data.value: Pulsepath is free for 3 sessions a week, with all the habit tracking. Plus has every session, rest-day planning and the weekly review for {0} a month or {1} a year. The first 14 days of Plus are free: cancel before day 14 and you pay nothing. Outside the euro area, the App Store sets the price in your currency.

data.name: Faq5Q
data.value: Is the web app the same as the iPhone app?

data.name: Faq5A
data.value: Same sessions, habits and streak, synced through your account. The web app can't read steps from Apple Health, so the steps habit is iPhone only. Reminders come as browser notifications.

data.name: Faq6Q
data.value: What happens to my health data?

data.name: Faq6A
data.value: Your sessions and habits are stored in the EU, in Frankfurt, and are never sold or shared with advertisers. There are no ads in Pulsepath. Steps from Apple Health stay on your iPhone; only the daily total shows in Today. You can export or delete everything from Settings.

data.name: Faq7Q
data.value: Can I use it with an injury?

data.name: Faq7A
data.value: Every move has an easier version, and you can mark knees, back or shoulders to keep sessions gentle on them. Pulsepath isn't medical advice: if you're recovering from an injury, check with a doctor or physiotherapist first.

data.name: AboutDescription
data.value: Pulsepath is a team of 14 in Copenhagen, started by a physiotherapist and an app developer in 2023. Why ten minutes, why rest days, and why iPhone first.

data.name: AboutLede
data.value: Pulsepath started in a physiotherapy clinic in Copenhagen, with patients who knew exactly what to do and never had an hour to do it.

data.name: AboutStory1
data.value: Freja Holm spent nine years as a physiotherapist in Nørrebro. Her patients left with a sheet of exercises and came back a month later having done them twice. The ones who got better had one thing in common: they did a little, most days.

data.name: AboutStory2
data.value: In 2023 she started writing ten-minute sessions on the back of appointment cards, and Kofi Mensah, a patient with a bad shoulder and a career in banking apps, offered to put them on a phone. The first version had 40 sessions and a timer.

data.name: AboutStory3
data.value: Inés Navarro joined a year later, after studying why people quit. Her answer was the streak that punishes one bad Tuesday, so Pulsepath has rest days instead.

data.name: AboutNumber2Label
data.value: of people who start are still training eight weeks later

data.name: AboutNumber3Label
data.value: people on the team, plus 3 physiotherapists who review every session

data.name: AboutNumber4Label
data.value: ads, now or later. Plus pays for everything.

data.name: Principle1Body
data.value: A session you do is worth more than the one you plan. Every session has a five-minute version for the bad days.

data.name: Principle2Title
data.value: Rest is part of the plan

data.name: Principle2Body
data.value: Two rest days a week, and no red crosses. Missing a day doesn't wipe out a month.

data.name: Principle3Body
data.value: Plus pays for Pulsepath. Your data is stored in the EU and never sold, and you can take it with you at any time.

data.name: Principle4Body
data.value: Three physiotherapists review each session before it ships, and every move has an easier version.

data.name: AboutLaunchBody
data.value: We're a small team, and we'd rather ship one app done well than two done halfway. The web app came next because people asked to train at their desks. Android is the one we're asked about most, and it's close.
